metadata.case_name: POON YAT CHIU v. AES SCAFFOLD ENGINEERING LTD

plaintiff.occupation_before: Driver as well as the operator of a crane truck
plaintiff.occupation_after: Part-time/full-time messenger (driving a private car with automatic transmission)

injuries.description: he was found to have a disc bulging at the L4/L5 level of his lower spine.
source: On 14 September 2003, the Plaintiff had an MRI examination, and he was found to have a disc bulging at the L4/L5 level of his lower spine.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis

injuries.description: lower back injury sustained in an alleged fall-from-height accident during work on 20th January 2003, resulting in lower back pain.
source: 8.1 Mr. Poon sustained lower back injury in an alleged fall-from-height accident during work on 20th January 2003. As a result he developed lower back pain.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of muscle, fascia or tendon of lower back

injuries.description: tenderness and superficial abrasion over right buttock, right shin and left hand.
injuries.body_part: right buttock; right shin; left hand
source: Medical examination conducted on him showed that there were tenderness and superficial abrasion over right buttock, right shin and left hand.

injuries.description: adjustment disorder (psychiatric condition) secondary to chronic back pain.
source: The Plaintiff was diagnosed to be suffering from adjustment disorder by Dr. K.M. Cheng of Castle Peak Hospital.

2. Mr. Poon did not have past or family history of mental illness. He was referred by Department of Orthropaedics and Traumatology, Tuen Mun Hospital, for poor sleep since his injury in January 2003 ……

3. He presented with poor sleep secondary to his chronic back pain, depressed and anxious mood, as well as easy irritability. He was treated as adjustment disorder. Pharmacological and psychological treatments were offered. He showed partial improvement of mood and sleep symptoms after treatment, despite his chronic pain.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis

manifestations.description: Chronic pain and associated impairment acting as a perpetuating factor for psychiatric problem
Tenderness and superficial abrasion over right buttock, right shin and left hand
Cannot sit or stand for too long; after about 15–20 minutes lower back, waist and bottom feel pins and needles pain and stiffness requiring him to stand up and move around
Poor sleep, depressed and anxious mood, easy irritability, partial improvement after treatment (adjustment disorder)
Pain on pressing the clutch of heavy vehicles preventing him from driving crane truck (difficulty performing clutch operation)
Avoids social interactions; reduced pleasure/enjoyment from usual activities

treatments_received: Sent to the Tuen Mun Hospital for treatment
Assessment and treatment at Castle Peak Hospital (psychiatric assessment by Dr. K.M. Cheng)
Pharmacological and psychological treatments (as offered by Castle Peak Hospital)
treatments_future: Professor Peter Lee recommended 5 sessions of psychotherapy (average cost stated as $1,500 per session in private sector)

losses.description: Cannot sit or stand for too long; after about 15–20 minutes lower back and bottom feel pins and needles pain and stiffness requiring him to stand up and move around.
Before the accident he led a very active social life; subsequently he avoids social interactions and has reduced pleasure/enjoyment from usual activities.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: He was highly sportive before the accident but has diminished ability to engage in sporting activities due to chronic back pain.
